title: Memory and Independence Worries
summary: How the person feels about their memory and managing daily tasks. This is not a memory test.
clinicianNotes: This is not a cognitive screen and cannot detect dementia. If worries are high, refer for a medical and cognitive assessment. Written for adults aged 60 and over. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

guidance.ok: On memory worries, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On memory worries, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Ask for specific examples and how long it has been noticed.
guidance.explore: On memory worries, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Ask for specific examples and how long it has been noticed.

domains.label: Confidence in daily tasks
domains.description: Feeling unsure managing money, medicines or places.

guidance.ok: On confidence in daily tasks, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On confidence in daily tasks, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore safety with money and medicines and what help is in place.
guidance.explore: On confidence in daily tasks, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore safety with money and medicines and what help is in place.

guidance.ok: On feelings about it, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On feelings about it, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore shame and what would make it easier to talk.
guidance.explore: On feelings about it, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore shame and what would make it easier to talk.

domains.label: Help and safety
domains.description: Having help, feeling safe and openness to seeing a doctor.

guidance.ok: On help and safety, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On help and safety, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on trusted helpers and willingness to be checked.
guidance.explore: On help and safety, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on trusted helpers and willingness to be checked.

items.text: I worry that my memory is getting worse.
I forget names, dates or where I put things more than before.
Other people have commented on my forgetfulness.
I feel unsure managing money or medicines.
I get lost or confused in places I know.
I avoid tasks I used to do because I fear mistakes.
Thinking about my memory makes me anxious or sad.
I feel embarrassed when I forget things.
I hide my memory problems from others.
Someone helps me with reminders or tasks when needed.
I would be willing to see a doctor about my memory.
